title: This Toothbrush Makes Its Own Electricity to Zap Bacteria
description:
Researchers at Peking University built a toothbrush whose bristles make their own electricity: they're made of PVDF, a plastic that builds up charge when it bends, which sparks reactions in saliva that create reactive oxygen molecules that damage bacteria.
In lab tests the bristles killed about 53% of a major cavity-causing bacterium vs 9% for nylon, and in a 3-month trial with 115 volunteers the brush beat nylon on plaque, gum inflammation and bleeding. Experts say more testing is needed. This is science news, not dental advice.
